subject: general
question: What is the equivalent resistance of a series combination of resistors?

options.text: The sum of the individual resistances.
The reciprocal of the sum of the individual resistances.
The product of the individual resistances.
The difference between the individual resistances.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The sum of the individual resistances.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When resistors are connected in series, the equivalent resistance is the sum of all individual resistances.
 
• This is because the current has only one path to take, and it flows through each resistor sequentially.
 
• The formula for the equivalent resistance Rₑq in a series circuit is Rₑq = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + .......+ R_n.
 
• In a series circuit, the total resistance increases with the addition of more resistors.
 
• This principle is essential for designing electrical circuits to control the total resistance and current flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is V=IR, where V is voltage, I is current and R is Resistance.
 
 
 
• **Series Circuit Characteristics:**
 
 
• In a series circuit, the same current flows through all components.
 
• The total voltage across the circuit is the sum of the voltages across each component.
 
• If one component fails, the entire circuit is broken.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Circuit:**
 
 
• In contrast to a series circuit, a parallel circuit has multiple paths for current to flow.
 
• The equivalent resistance of parallel resistors is less than the smallest individual resistor.
 
• The formula for the equivalent resistance Rₚ in a parallel circuit is (1)/(R_p)=(1)/(R₁)+(1)/(R₂)+.......+(1)/(R_n)
 
 
 
• **Applications of Series Circuits:**
 
 
• Series circuits are used in applications where the current must be the same through all components, such as in string lights.
 
• They are also used in voltage divider circuits, which are used to create reference voltages.
